grand_strategy.reading: The Union acts as a grand strategist only by accident. It has no army, no single voice and no budget that anyone loves; what it has is a market, a rulebook, a currency and the right to say yes or no to its neighbours. Read through Luttwak, that is a strategy of the second level: it exports order by attraction (enlargement, association, Growth Plan money, visa-free travel) and by exclusion (sanctions, frozen assets, trade defence), and it moves only when 27 governments consent. In 2026 the logic of consent has hardened into a posture: Russia is the declared threat, the United States has become a 'necessary partner' that cannot be left and cannot be trusted, China is a rival managed through quotas and licences, and the neighbourhood is a queue. The paradoxes all come from the same root - the Union is strongest where its rules are least contested and most exposed where it needs speed. It has just shown it can finance a war (EUR 90bn), outlast a spoiler (Orban's defeat on 12 Apr 2026) and ban a fuel (Russian gas), and it still cannot appoint an envoy, use the assets it froze or guarantee its own borders without Washington. The reading for the next year is whether the Ankara-era bargain - a more European NATO, a Union that pays - turns into capacity, or whether the 2028-34 budget, the Turnberry steel clause and the Hungarian reversal are only a pause.

stances.note: The Union cooperates with Washington out of necessity - the guarantee, US LNG (26.2% of EU gas imports in 2025, 57.9% of LNG), the largest trade partner - while resisting alignment: Turnberry fixed a 15% US tariff ceiling on 27 Jul 2025 but the steel and aluminium duties stayed at up to 50% (the Parliament added a sunrise clause, a suspension right and a sunset); in Jan 2026 Trump threatened 10% then 25% tariffs on eight European states over Greenland and Brussels readied EUR 93bn of counter-tariffs without triggering the Anti-Coercion Instrument; Washington attacked the EUR 120m DSA fine on X. Not reluctant_ally: the EU has no treaty with the US (the guarantee is NATO's, graded separately). Not rival: no one in Brussels seeks the US's defeat, and ECFR's May 2026 poll finds half of Europeans calling it a 'necessary partner', only 11% an ally. Cooling: US troop-review and the 22 Sep 2026 US-Denmark Greenland deal followed the Ankara summit. Bond - affinity: values and history, strained.
